AWD stands for all-wheel drive. It's a drivetrain that sends power to all four wheels, either full-time or automatically when the system detects slip, which helps with traction on wet roads, snow, or loose surfaces. It's different from 4WD, which is typically a more rugged system, often with selectable modes, found on trucks and larger SUVs.

results.say: do you think a jeep is good in chicago winters?
results.reply:
Generally, yes. Many Jeep models come with 4WD or AWD and have decent ground clearance, which helps in deep snow and slushy side streets. Keep in mind that AWD and 4WD help you get going, not stop, so good winter tires matter more than the badge on the back. A Wrangler is very capable in snow but can feel lighter and noisier on windy, icy highways, while a Grand Cherokee or Compass tends to ride more smoothly day to day.
